Population pressure on land – Sharp fall in agriculture's employment share in the Plan era
Colonial deindustrialisation – Pushed artisans onto the land
Capital-intensive growth – Rapid movement of workers out of farming
x: Colonial deindustrialisation pushed artisans onto the land; capital-intensive growth failed to absorb surplus farm labour, and agriculture's share fell only marginally in the Plan era.

s: In which period did jobless growth become especially evident in India?
x: In the late 1990s, employment growth fell to early-plan levels even while GDP kept growing.

s: What does 'jobless growth' refer to?
o: Output grows without a matching rise in quality employment
Employment shifts from agriculture to services
x: Jobless growth is output growth not matched by adequate employment growth, especially in formal, quality jobs.

s: According to an RBI study (2014), in which sector is employment elasticity negative?
x: Employment elasticity is negative in agriculture; construction and services are the most employment-intensive.

s: Only about what share of India's workers had formal vocational training?
x: Only 4.2% had formal vocational training, slowing the shift out of agriculture.

s: Which historical factor pushed Indian artisans onto the land?
x: Colonial deindustrialisation pushed artisans onto land, one reason for the slow shift out of agriculture.

s: According to an RBI study (2014), which of the following is among the most employment-intensive sectors?
x: Construction and services are the most employment-intensive; employment elasticity in agriculture is negative.

s: In which law was a 'gig worker' defined for the first time?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (Section 2(35)) first defined a gig worker.

s: Gig workers form about what share of India's 61.6 crore workforce?
x: Gig workers are about 2% of the workforce.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about gig and platform work in India?
o: Gig workers earn outside the traditional employer-employee relationship
Platform work uses an online platform to reach others or provide services
Gig workers are a separate category in the PLFS
A gig worker is defined in Section 2(35) of the Code on Social Security, 2020
x: Gig workers are not yet a separate PLFS category; the other statements are correct.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Structural unemployment — industry, urban and educated workers
Frictional unemployment — agricultural sowing and harvesting seasons
x: Frictional unemployment refers to a temporary period between jobs and is linked with the urban or organised sector. Work confined to sowing and harvesting seasons is seasonal unemployment in agriculture.

s: A trained worker loses a job because new technology needs skills the worker does not have. Which type of unemployment is this?
x: Structural unemployment results from a mismatch between available skills and job requirements caused by technology or broader structural change. It is associated with industry, urban areas and educated workers.

s: What is the unemployment in which extra workers have marginal productivity near zero called?
x: Disguised unemployment means more people than needed, with marginal productivity near zero, mainly in agriculture.

s: What type of unemployment occurs during a short gap between leaving one job and joining another?
x: Frictional unemployment is a short gap between jobs; skill mismatch is structural.

s: What is unemployment caused by a mismatch between skills and jobs called?
x: Structural unemployment is a skills-jobs mismatch; frictional is a short gap between jobs and cyclical follows a business-cycle slump.

s: What type of unemployment is caused by a fall in demand during a business-cycle slump?
x: Cyclical unemployment rises when demand falls in a slump; it is linked with industry.

s: Which one of the following is most closely associated with a high share of 'other workers', particularly in services?
o: Chhattisgarh, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh
x: Urbanised Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have high shares of other workers, including service-sector workers.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Census 2011 is correctly matched?
x: In Census 2011 cultivators were 14.5% of AP's workers (India 24.7%); all agricultural workers were 62.4% in AP and 54.6% in India.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, in what ratio do agricultural labourers outnumber cultivators?
x: In AP labourers outnumbered cultivators about 3:1, against about 1.2:1 for India.

s: As per PLFS 2023-24, what share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was in agriculture?
x: Agriculture was 45.6 per cent of AP employment, close to India's 46.1 per cent.

s: Which of the following comparisons regarding rural casual labour is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh recorded 33.8%, compared with India's 22.5%.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 40.2%, compared with India's 18.7%.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 18.7%, compared with India's 40.2%.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 22.5%, compared with India's 33.8%.
x: Rural casual labour constituted 33.8% in Andhra Pradesh compared with 22.5% in India.

s: In 2026, rural female LFPR gains were led by which States?
o: West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
x: Rural female LFPR gains were led by West Bengal, UP and Bihar; urban gains by Rajasthan and Gujarat.

s: Which Census worker category is large in urbanised Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry?
x: Urbanised areas have most workers in services, trade and factories, which the Census calls 'other workers'.

s: As per Census 2011, what percentage of Andhra Pradesh's workers were agricultural labourers?
x: In AP (13 districts) agricultural labourers were 47.9% of workers, against 30.0% in India.

s: As per Census 2011, what share of Andhra Pradesh's workers were in agriculture (cultivators and agricultural labourers together)?
x: 62.4% of AP's workers were in agriculture, above India's 54.6%.

s: As per PLFS 2023-24, what was the youth (15-29 years) unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's overall unemployment rate was 4.1%, but youth unemployment was 17.5%.

s: As per Census 2011, which State had the highest share of cultivators among its workers?
x: Himachal Pradesh had the highest share of cultivators among workers (57.9%) in Census 2011.

s: As per Census 2011, which State had the highest share of agricultural labourers among its workers?
x: Bihar had the highest share of agricultural labourers among workers (52.8%) in Census 2011.

s: What annual growth rate does the 'Hindu rate of growth' refer to?
x: It refers to about 3.5% a year (3.52% during 1950-1980), not 5.5%.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Growth before Independence — approximately 1 per cent annually
Industry during the Plan era — approximately 0.3 per cent growth
Agriculture during the Plan era — approximately 2–3 per cent growth
Plans I–XI — approximately 4.5 per cent annual growth
x: Industrial growth during the Plan era was approximately 6–8 per cent, not 0.3 per cent. The figure of 0.3 per cent refers to agricultural growth before Independence.

s: What was the main livelihood of India's people on the eve of Independence?
x: Agriculture was the main livelihood at Independence, though it grew only 0.3% a year.

s: What was India's annual economic growth rate before Independence?
x: Growth before Independence was about 1% a year; 0.3% was the growth of agriculture alone.

s: At what annual rate did the Indian economy grow during the Plan era (Plans 1-11)?
x: The Plan era averaged about 4.5% a year, with agriculture at 2-3% and industry at 6-8%.

s: What was the average annual growth rate of the Indian economy during 1980-81 to 1989-90?
x: The average growth rate during 1980–81 to 1989–90 was in the range of 5.13 to 5.18 per cent.

s: During which period did the Indian economy record its post-reform peak growth rate of 8.5 per cent?
x: Growth peaked at 8.5 per cent during 2003–08; post-reform growth averaged about 6.5 per cent.

s: What growth rate did Andhra Pradesh record in 2025-26, against India's 7.4 per cent?
x: AP grew 9.88 per cent against India's 7.4 per cent, and has outgrown India in most years since 2014–15.

s: What did ex-CEA Arvind Subramanian estimate India's growth during 2011-17 to be?
o: 4.5 per cent rather than 7 per cent
8.5 per cent rather than 7 per cent
6.5 per cent rather than 4.5 per cent
3.5 per cent rather than 6.8 per cent
x: Arvind Subramanian placed India’s growth during 2011–17 at approximately 4.5 per cent, rather than the reported 7 per cent.

s: What was India's growth rate in 2025-26 (provisional estimate)?
x: Post-Covid growth was 7.2% (2023-24), 7.1% (2024-25) and 7.7% (2025-26 PE); 6.6% is the RBI outlook for 2026-27.

s: What growth rate did the RBI project for India in 2026-27 (June 2026)?
x: The RBI expected growth to slow to 6.6% in 2026-27, from 7.7% in 2025-26.

s: What was the main cause of the -5.8 per cent contraction in 2020-21?
x: 2020-21 recorded -5.8% due to the Covid-19 pandemic, the worst contraction since independence.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: 1979-80 recorded -5.2% and 2020-21 -5.8%; 2003-08 was the 8.5% peak phase.

s: In which year did India record a growth rate of -5.2 per cent?
x: 1979-80 saw -5.2% due to drought and the second oil shock; 2020-21 saw -5.8%.

s: Which of the following statements about the Hindu Rate of Growth is incorrect?
o: It refers to India’s slow rate of growth of National Income or GDP.
The term was coined by economist Raj Krishna.
It was associated with the period from the 1950s to the early 1980s.
It referred to an approximate growth rate of around 5.5%.
x: Option D is incorrect: the Hindu rate of growth was about 3.5% a year, not 5.5%. It describes the 1950s to the early 1980s.

s: Which period does the 'Hindu rate of growth' describe?
x: It describes the stagnant growth of the 1950s to the early 1980s; it was broken in the 1980s.

s: Under the 'Hindu rate of growth', at what annual rate did India's per capita income grow?
x: Per capita growth was only 1.37% a year, barely above population growth; 3.5% was the overall growth rate.

s: In which year did Prof. Raj Krishna coin the term 'Hindu rate of growth'?
x: Raj Krishna coined the term in 1978 for India's slow growth of about 3.5% a year.

s: Which term about the Indian economy was coined by Prof. Raj Krishna?
x: Raj Krishna used 'Hindu rate of growth' to describe India's stagnant GDP growth of about 3.5% from the 1950s to early 1980s.

s: What is the 8%+ growth hoped for through AI-led 'Reforms 3.0' called (June 2026)?
x: The 'Bharat rate of growth' of 8%+ is a 2026 echo of the old 'Hindu rate of growth'.

s: Who coined the term ‘Hindu rate of growth’ to describe India's low and stagnant growth of roughly 3.5 per cent during the 1950s–1980s?
x: Raj Krishna coined the term ‘Hindu rate of growth’ for India's stagnant or low growth of about 3.5 per cent during the period.

s: In the view that treats 1991 as the turning point, in which event did the debt-fuelled growth of the 1980s end?
x: The 1980s growth phase is seen as debt-fuelled and unstable, ending in the 1991 crisis, after which sustained high growth began.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The 1991 crisis was a balance-of-payments crisis, with foreign exchange reserves sufficient for only about two weeks of imports. The East Asian financial crisis caused the slowdown of 1997–98.

s: During the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis, for how long could India's foreign exchange reserves pay for imports?
x: Reserves covered only about two weeks of imports, and the fiscal deficit had reached 8.4% in 1990; the crisis led to the July 1991 reforms.

s: With which event was India's slowdown of 1997-98 linked?
x: The 1997-98 slowdown came with the East Asian financial crisis.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1991 crisis:
1. Foreign exchange reserves could pay for only about two weeks of imports.
2. India's fiscal deficit in 1990 was about 8.4%.
3. It was caused by the East Asian financial crisis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: In 1991 reserves covered only two weeks of imports after debt-fuelled growth with a fiscal deficit of 8.4%; the East Asian crisis came later, in 1997-98.

s: Which event of 1990-91 sharply raised India's oil import bill and cut remittances, draining forex reserves before the 1991 crisis?
x: The 1990-91 Gulf War pushed up oil prices and cut remittances from Indian workers in the Gulf, draining reserves.

s: How did Rodrik and Subramanian (2004) describe the attitudinal shift behind India's growth transition around 1980?
x: They called the 1980s shift pro-business, not pro-market; DeLong (2003) also placed the take-off in the 1980s.

s: Who placed India's growth take-off in the 1980s, before the 1991 reforms, in a 2003 study?
x: DeLong (2003) argued the take-off came in the 1980s, before 1991; Rodrik-Subramanian also dated it to about 1980.

s: What was India's fiscal deficit in 1990, before the 1991 crisis?
x: The debt-fuelled 1980s ended with a fiscal deficit of 8.4% in 1990, leading to the 1991 crisis.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the turning-point debate?
o: Rodrik-Subramanian dated the transition to about 1980
x: Rodrik and Subramanian called the 1980 shift pro-business, not pro-market.

s: Which of the following milestones came first?
x: Pantnagar came in 1960, before the Green Revolution phase (1966-67), bank nationalisation (1969) and the first KVK (1974).

s: In which year was the State Bank of India set up?
x: SBI dates from 1955; the Community Development Programme was 1952, the Second Industrial Policy 1956 and IDBI 1964.

s: In what context did the Third Plan fail and the Plan Holiday of 1966-69 follow?
o: The East Asian financial crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic
The second oil shock and the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis
Bank nationalisation and the Green Revolution
Wars with China and Pakistan and severe droughts
x: The wars of 1962 and 1965, along with severe droughts in 1965–66, contributed to the failure of the Third Plan and the Plan Holiday of 1966–69.

s: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India nationalised on 1 January?
x: RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949; IFCI came in 1948 and the First Plan in 1951.

s: In which year was the First Finance Commission constituted?
x: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 under Article 280, with K.C. Neogy as Chairman.

s: By how much was the Indian rupee devalued on 6 June 1966?
x: The rupee was devalued by 36.5% on 6 June 1966 amid BoP stress after war and drought.

s: How many banks were nationalised in July 1969?
x: Fourteen banks were nationalised in July 1969 to extend credit to agriculture and priority sectors.

s: Who was the chairman of the First Finance Commission (1951)?
x: The First Finance Commission under Article 280 was chaired by K.C. Neogy.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1966-69 period:
1. The rupee was devalued by 36.5% on 6 June 1966.
2. A Plan Holiday followed the failure of the Third Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the rupee was devalued by 36.5% in June 1966, and wars and droughts that failed the Third Plan led to the 1966-69 Plan Holiday.

s: In which year was the first National Planning Committee set up?
x: The first National Planning Committee was set up in 1938.

s: In which year was the Community Development Programme launched?
x: The Community Development Programme began in 1952, a year after the First Plan.

s: Which two institutions were set up in 1964?
x: IDBI and UTI were set up in 1964; SBI and ICICI in 1955.

s: The IRDP was tried experimentally in 1978-79. In which year was it implemented nationwide?
x: IRDP went national in 1980, the year of the second bank nationalisation.

s: In which year was the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) set up?
x: The first KVK dates from 1974; the first RRB was 1975, NABARD 1982 and the first private mutual fund 1993.

s: In which year did Indira Gandhi raise the slogan 'Garibi Hatao'?
x: 'Garibi Hatao' was raised in 1971, not 1969, the year 14 banks were nationalised.

s: In which year was the National Rural Employment Programme launched?
x: NREP came in 1980; IDBI was 1964, the Dandekar–Rath study 1971 and the first Food-for-Work programme 1977–78.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SIDBI was set up in 1990. DWCRA dates from 1982, JRY from 1989 and the New Economic Policy from 1991.

s: The First Human Development Report was published in which year?
x: The UNDP published the first Human Development Report in 1990, prepared by Mahbub-ul-Haq.

s: Which was the first Regional Rural Bank in India (1975)?
x: The first RRB, set up in 1975, was Prathama Grameen Bank.

s: In which year was NABARD set up?
x: NABARD was set up in 1982, along with DWCRA.

s: In which year did the second round of bank nationalisation take place?
x: Banks were first nationalised in 1969 (14 banks) and a second round followed in 1980.

Arrange the following in chronological order:

s: Which study on poverty in India appeared in 1971, the year of 'Garibi Hatao'?
x: The Dandekar-Rath poverty study came in 1971, when poverty removal became a national goal.

s: In which State did the Antyodaya programme begin in 1977-78?
x: Antyodaya began in Rajasthan in 1977-78, along with the first Food-for-Work programme.

s: In which year did the first private-sector mutual fund come up in India?
x: The first private-sector mutual fund came in 1993, after the 1991 reforms.

s: Who is associated with the first Human Development Report of the UNDP (1990)?
x: The first Human Development Report (UNDP, 1990) was led by Mahbub-ul-Haq.

s: Why is the Bombay Plan (1944) significant?
o: Industrialists opposed all forms of state intervention.
The state transferred all industries to foreign companies.
The private sector demanded abolition of industrial licensing in 1944.
Industrialists themselves sought state protection and planning support.
x: The Bombay Plan of 1944 was prepared by industrialists who themselves sought state protection, making the Licence Raj partly a capitalist demand.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, Schedule B listed how many industries?
x: Schedule B listed 12 industries; Schedule A reserved 17 for the State, cut to 8 in 1991.

s: What was India's main policy orientation between 1947 and 1991?
o: Import substitution with a large public-sector role
Free trade with minimal state intervention
x: The policy orientation was import substitution backed by state planning and public investment, not export promotion or deregulation.

s: Under the 1991 reforms, industries reserved for the public sector were reduced from 17 to how many?
x: The 1991 reforms cut the reserved list (Schedule A of IPR 1956) from 17 to 8.

s: Under the pro-business reforms of the 1980s, to what level was the MRTP asset limit raised?
x: The 1980s reforms raised the MRTP limit to Rs 100 crore, with broad-banding of licences and tax cuts.

s: Which Five Year Plan adopted import substitution as its strategy?
x: The Third Plan (1961-66) adopted import substitution as the strategy.

s: Which industrial policy is called the 'Economic Constitution' of India?
x: The IPR 1956, with Schedule A (17) and Schedule B (12) industries, is called India's Economic Constitution.

s: Which financial institution was set up in 1948, the year of India's first Industrial Policy?
x: The first Industrial Policy (1948) was followed by the setting up of the IFCI the same year.

s: What is the Incremental Capital-Output Ratio (ICOR)?
o: Change in output ÷ change in capital
Change in output ÷ change in labour
Change in capital ÷ change in output
x: ICOR is the extra capital needed per unit of extra output; a lower ICOR means more efficient investment.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Second Five Year Plan?
o: Investment was raised from 7% to 11% of national income
Long gestation periods contributed to a high ICOR
It emphasised light, labour-intensive consumer industries
The high ICOR kept growth lower than expected
x: The Second Plan emphasised heavy and capital-intensive industries.

s: In the Harrod-Domar model, with the savings rate unchanged, what does a rise in the capital-output ratio do?
o: First raise and then lower the growth rate
x: Since g = s/k, a higher capital-output ratio lowers growth when the savings rate is unchanged.

s: What does a lower Incremental Capital-Output Ratio (ICOR) indicate?
x: ICOR is change in capital divided by change in output; a lower ICOR means more efficient investment.

s: About what share of India's GDP was gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) in 2025-26?
x: GFCF was about 30% of GDP in 2025-26; net household financial savings were about 5.3% of GDP.
